name: US–China / Taiwan
value: Peace declaration 19 Nov; no clash or blockade
summary: Trump, Xi and Putin issued a nuclear-risk declaration in Shenzhen on 19 Nov; disputes over chip controls continue
state: Trump, Xi and Putin met in Shenzhen on 19 Nov and issued a declaration that a nuclear war cannot be won, with a dialogue on nuclear risks but no timetable. It did not mention Taiwan or trade, and Wang Yi said working-level coordination would continue (Reuters via GMA News). Before the talks, Xi had complained about new US high-tech export controls and US prosecutors had opened an inquiry into the alleged diversion of Nvidia chips to China (Al Jazeera, 18 Nov). No blockade, military clash or severed channel was found, and Watch holds on the export-control dispute.
for_you: Supply chains for chips, electronics and goods that depend on rare earths are the most exposed to US–China friction. The FCDO publishes travel advice for China and Taiwan.
rubric_hit: Watch: major new US export controls (16 Nov chip restrictions) still in dispute; no blockade, clash or severed channel for Alert

why: The world's two largest economies; a Taiwan crisis would halt most advanced chip supply and risk great-power war.
drivers: PLA exercises, tariffs and tech controls, diplomacy, Taiwan politics, South China Sea incidents.

rubric.alert: Blockade or 'quarantine' of Taiwan, military clash, or severed diplomatic channels.
rubric.watch: Large-scale PLA exercises around Taiwan, major new sanctions/controls, or a naval/air incident.
rubric.normal: Managed relations; dialogue channels open; routine PLA activity.
